title: What Do All Parties Expect in This Cooperative Election?
translatorNote: This translation is intended to carry Kalaignar's voice into clear, contemporary English rather than recast the letter as literary or academic prose. It preserves the source's argument, political directness, rhetorical questions, repetition, irony, factual detail, and paragraph order. Names, dates, figures, quotations, and intentional English expressions are retained. Where Tamil idiom cannot be reproduced literally without sounding unnatural, the English follows its sense and rhetorical force without adding claims absent from the source. The original Tamil is reproduced in full below the translation and remains the authoritative text. `Udanpirappē` is retained in Tamil transliteration rather than flattened into “brother,” “sister,” or “comrade.” Literally evoking “one born alongside me,” Kalaignar uses it as a distinctive address of shared identity, equality, affection, and solidarity within the movement. Letter-specific notes: 1. **CITU** is retained as the trade-union acronym used in the source; **Puthiya Tamilagam** is transliterated from the party name. 2. The source-visible leading full stop before `செய்வதில்` on PDF 229 remains preserved in the authoritative Tamil below; it is not silently used to alter the English meaning. 3. Reports of violence, intimidation and misconduct remain attributed to the named political statements and newspapers or are presented as the author's account, rather than converted into independently verified findings.
paragraphs: Elections are said to be taking place for cooperative societies in Tamil Nadu. Anticipating in advance how the AIADMK government would conduct itself in those elections, the Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam had already decided not to participate in the cooperative elections and openly announced that decision in a statement. Even so, some members of other parties and some people not affiliated with any party concluded that the AIADMK government might at least make some attempt to conduct the elections properly, and they are contesting here and there.

But reports continue to appear every day about what they are being made to suffer because of the AIADMK government's anti-democratic actions, and about ruling-party factions themselves getting into internecine brawls in places during these cooperative elections. I have already written about this two or three times. Yet, so that the people of the State may understand the injustices produced by the continuing abuse of authority by ruling-party members, I have gathered some of them here.

In a statement published in Theekkathir dated 16 April 2013, G. Ramakrishnan, State Secretary of the Communist Party of India (Marxist), said that the CPI(M) State Executive had already condemned the widespread excesses of the ruling party in the first two phases of elections to cooperative bodies, criticised the Election Commission for remaining a mere spectator, and urged the Commission to ensure that the cooperative elections were conducted honestly and democratically.

He continued that when nominations were filed in Chennai for the third phase, in many places parties other than the ruling party, organisations and individuals were not allowed to file nominations. In many places, the police could be seen acting in support of the ruling party's lawlessness. Ruling-party members locked the doors of offices where nominations were to be filed and refused to let others enter; they gathered in groups and threatened and attacked people with weapons including bicycle chains and knives. Comrades who, unable even to enter to submit nominations and facing attacks, fought to uphold democratic rights were surrounded and arrested. He said this was the situation at many societies, including the T. Nagar Cooperative Bank, Pallavan Transport Corporation Employees Cooperative Credit Society, Transport Corporation Employees Credit Society, Anna Labour Cooperative Society, Nochikuppam Fishermen's Society and Fishermen's Credit Cooperative Society, and that the CPI(M) strongly condemned these atrocious anti-democratic acts.

Another report on the cooperative elections said AIADMK members did not allow other candidates to file nominations; only AIADMK members filed nominations for all positions. Road blockades were held in protest against the ruling party's lawless conduct. Police baton-charged the protesters and rounded them up for arrest. Such incidents occurred in T. Nagar, Teynampet, Royapettah, Tambaram, Nochikuppam, Pallavan Illam and Broadway. CITU organised blockade protests in various places against them.

A statement issued by CITU on the cooperative elections said: “The Anna DMK trade union came with a gang of more than a thousand rowdies armed with sticks, bicycle chains and knives, attacked CITU candidates who were standing in line to file nominations, and openly drove them out of the office.”

In some places in these cooperative elections, AIADMK members themselves split into two groups and clashed. For example, in Tiruvallur, 24 people separately filed nominations under the leadership of AIADMK district councillor Kumar and former AIADMK union committee chairman Jayaraman. During polling, an argument arose between booth agents, developed into physical fighting, and the two sides threw stones at each other, injuring several people. The Inspector's car windows, four motorcycles and an autorickshaw were smashed.
More than a hundred AIADMK members led by Govindaraj, who contested in the cooperative election, staged a road blockade on the Sholinghur–Chittoor road.
Journalists who went to photograph polling at the Tiruporur Union Primary School were chased away, after which the election results were announced.

At Gandhipuram A.T.T. Colony in Coimbatore, there is a women's garment producers' cooperative society. More than 300 women voters there were not even given an opportunity to vote. Their arguments with those conducting the election produced no result.

While voting was under way at the Udayanatham Primary Agricultural Cooperative Credit Society in Ariyalur, some unidentified persons entered, snatched ballot papers and tore them up. A blockade protest was held there over this.

In the election to the Anaikkudam Primary Agricultural Cooperative Credit Society, unidentified persons entered the polling station, snatched the ballot paper from election officer Pandian and tore it up.
In the election to the Kodalikaruppur Primary Agricultural Cooperative Credit Society, ruling-party members tried to enter the polling booth, a dispute broke out, and the election was suspended.

The 16 April 2013 issue of Dina Thanthi itself published photographs from the previous day's nomination filing in the Dindigul cooperative election, where a clash broke out and AIADMK members and CITU trade-union members attacked one another with sticks; it also carried a photograph of an injured person walking away with blood dripping from his wounds. They were attacking one another even in the presence of the police. Dina Thanthi reported that Manikandan, Abhimanyu, Anwar, Masanam, Mohammed Ali Jinnah, Chinnapparaj, Muthusamy, Satishkumar, Manickam, Jayakumar, Raja and Savarinathan were injured in stone-throwing and attacks with wooden clubs and were being treated at Dindigul Government Hospital.

A report published in Dinamalar on 16 April 2013 carried a photograph of a clash between CPI(M) members who had come to the T. Nagar cooperative office to file nominations for cooperative-society elections and AIADMK members.
It also carried a report with a photograph of one faction staging a road blockade after a dispute arose between two ruling-party groups over filing nominations at Kasimedu in Chennai.

On the 16th, when the Communist parties and Puthiya Tamilagam tried in the Assembly to raise the issue of irregularities in the cooperative elections, our Speaker—who conducts the House impartially and without party bias—magnanimously said: “The Minister has already replied to the demand for grants for the Cooperation Department; I cannot permit the cooperative election to be discussed again.” The Electricity Minister, meanwhile, told the House that five members of his own party had been seriously injured in clashes arising from the cooperative election and were undergoing treatment. From that alone one can understand how far the clashes in the cooperative election had escalated into violence.
Because the Speaker denied permission, the Communist parties and Puthiya Tamilagam walked out of the House.

In this manner, two phases of elections to cooperative bodies in Tamil Nadu have been completed. In those elections too, the AIADMK indulged in every kind of excess and violation of legal rules, carried out a murder of democracy, and ensured that only members of that party captured all the posts.
The Election Commission established by the AIADMK government to conduct these cooperative elections has been quietly watching and encouraging this farce every day.

After all this, at least now the Cooperative Election Commission must intervene and order the cancellation of all cooperative-society elections conducted in a lawless and illegal manner; it must accept nominations from everyone who wishes to file them democratically and then arrange for elections to be held. Proper action must be taken against ruling-party members who, intoxicated with power, took the law into their own hands and acted against democracy, and against police personnel who assisted them. Only then can it be announced to the country that the cooperative elections were properly conducted.

Every opposition party in Tamil Nadu has expressed this same view. This is what the people of Tamil Nadu too expect. Otherwise, there can be no meaning at all in having conducted these cooperative elections.
With affection, M.K. 18 April 2013
